title: Why Getariako Txakolina tastes the way it does

lede.text: 95% of the vineyards are less than 1 km from the sea. The wine is a fresh, light Txakoli, characteristic of this zone.

terms.text: The wine must have fermented, and turned from must to wine, in barrels.
A wine sold under one grape's name must contain at least 85% of a recommended variety.
A rosé must be made with at least 50% of the recommended red variety.
The place name Getaria may go with this term for wines from overripe grapes, with at least 12% alcohol.
The place name Getaria may be used for sparkling wine from registered vineyards, made in registered wineries.

chapters.title: Vines by the sea
paras: The zone is the province of Gipuzkoa. Before 2007 the zone was only three municipalities.
In the 19th century nearly all of the province's vines retreated to the coast at Getaria and Zarautz. Getaria kept 35 hectares in sheltered spots, and Zarautz kept 4.

chapters.title: Mild, wet and maritime
paras: The climate is mild Atlantic, with a maritime influence.
The average temperature is 13.4 °C. The average high is 16.4 °C and the average low is 10.5 °C.
Rain averages 1,600 mm a year and falls on 185 days. Clear sun lasts 1,800 hours a year.
There is no risk of spring frost.
Late summer and early autumn bring winds from the south and southwest. They make the air dry and warm.

chapters.title: Hard layers, soft layers
paras: Hard layers of limestone and sandstone alternate with soft layers of marl and clay rock.
Soil textures are mostly clay-loam or loam. The pH is usually neutral.
The wet climate grows thick vegetation. It protects the soil from erosion. It helps biological life, which enriches the soil with organic matter.
Most vineyards are on slopes sheltered from the northwest winds. The average slope is 15 to 20%. Growers always look for the most sun, for the best ripening.

chapters.title: Ondarrabi Zuri on a pergola
paras: Nearly all of the protected wine is white. Red and rosé are a small remainder.
The recommended grapes are Ondarrabi Zuri for white and Ondarrabi Beltza for red. Four other white grapes are authorised.
Yields are capped at 13,000 kg of grapes per hectare. Extraction is capped at 0.72 litres per kilo, or 93 hl of wine per hectare.

Vines are traditionally trained on pergolas, 80% of the registered vineyard. Ondarrabi Zuri is very vigorous, so it needs long pruning. On a pergola the bunches hang in the air, away from the damp of the soil.
The wine is traditionally made on its lees, with temperature control. It keeps part of its natural CO2.
The result is a fresh, light Txakoli. Strength is around 11.5% and acidity is above 7 g/l as tartaric.
